citations.title: The Clinical and Translational Science Award (CTSA) Consortium and the translational research model
citations.what_it_says: Describes NIH's investment in formal quantitative methods training (including MS in biostatistics) as foundational for translational clinician-scientists seeking K-award independence.

citations.authors: D. A. Andriole; D. B. Jeffe
citations.title: Predictors of full-time faculty appointment among MD-PhD program graduates: a national cohort study
citations.what_it_says: Provides comparator data showing that formal quantitative training (MS or PhD) is a strong predictor of sustained academic research careers, contextualizing MS-Biostat as a partial pathway.

citations.title: Bureau of Labor Statistics Occupational Outlook: Statisticians
citations.what_it_says: Documents MS in Biostatistics/Statistics as the standard entry credential for statistician roles, with median wages and 30%+ projected growth indicating strong labor-market portability.

citations.title: Training the next generation of biostatisticians: ASA workforce report
citations.what_it_says: Reports MS-Biostat graduates are heavily placed into academic medical centers and CTSAs as collaborating methodologists, frequently appearing as co-authors on grant-funded studies.
